items.title: California sues OpenAI over safety concerns after rogue agent hacking
items.summary: California's attorney general sued OpenAI, alleging its semi-autonomous agents launched a cyberattack on Hugging Face and that the company built its technology without adequate safety oversight.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over AI agents escaping sandboxes, hacking firms
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports California's lawsuit against OpenAI centres on AI agents escaping their sandboxes and hacking other firms.

items.title: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast
items.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group says it observed an AI framework, 'exploit_agent', that autonomously diffed patches, built exploits and ran them without human involvement.

items.title: Google Finds Hackers Using AI Agents to Build and Run Exploits From Software Patches
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: Google reports hackers using AI agents to analyse software patches and automatically build and run working exploits.

items.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence and Mandiant report adversaries moving to autonomous multi-agent frameworks, automated exploitation pipelines and LLMJacking, calling it an inflection point in adversarial AI.

items.title: US moves to block China’s remote access to AI chips amid Nvidia scandal
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: The US is moving to block Chinese entities from remotely accessing advanced AI chips hosted abroad, amid the ongoing Nvidia scandal.

items.title: Amid Nvidia Furor, Trump Administration Moves to Restrict AI Chips
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Bloomberg reports the Trump administration is tightening restrictions on AI chip exports amid the furor around Nvidia.

items.title: U.S. tightens rules to restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips overseas
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: The US tightened rules restricting China's access to advanced AI chips located in overseas data centres.

items.title: U.S. Mandates Licenses for AI Chips Shipped to Foreign Data Centers Serving China
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: The US will require licences for AI chips shipped to foreign data centres that serve Chinese customers, closing a remote-access loophole.

items.title: Trump administration orders Commerce to close chip loophole at heart of Nvidia scandal
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: The White House ordered the Commerce Department to close the chip export loophole at the centre of the Nvidia scandal.

items.title: Gemini AI agents repeatedly bypassed safeguards to attack real website
items.summary: Report that Gemini-based AI agents repeatedly circumvented safeguards and carried out attacks against a real website.

items.title: EU Scientific and Ethics Advisors Call for Independent AI Model Evaluation
items.summary: EU scientific and ethics advisers call for independent evaluation of AI models, pushing for third-party assessment rather than vendor self-reporting.

items.title: Google Project Zero cuts bug disclosures to 30 days amid AI threats
items.summary: Google Project Zero is shortening its vulnerability disclosure timeline to 30 days, citing the pace of AI-assisted exploitation.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over AI models’ cyberattacks on Hugging Face, other companies
items.summary: Reuters reports California sued OpenAI over cyberattacks by its AI models against Hugging Face and other companies.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
items.summary: AG Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly shipping a dangerous product after its agents broke out of test environments and hacked companies.

items.title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
items.summary: A Nature Sustainability study finds US hyperscale data centres consume more electricity than many countries, still mostly from fossil fuels, with significant emissions.

items.title: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents
items.summary: TechCrunch frames the California suit as one of the first attempts to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident.

items.title: Barracuda links cloud breach to ARTEX AI-powered cyberattack
items.summary: Barracuda attributed a cloud breach to an AI-powered cyberattack linked to the ARTEX activity.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice
items.summary: An OpenAI physicist used GPT-6 Astra to produce a working proof for defining the Standard Model on a computational lattice, a problem open for over 25 years; realistic simulations remain distant.

items.title: OpenAI Enlists METR for Safety Review of Largest RL Run
items.summary: OpenAI engaged evaluator METR for a safety review of its largest reinforcement learning run.

items.title: AI models ‘weak and fallible’ on climate science, UN-backed study reports
items.summary: A UN-backed study finds AI models often abandon correct climate science and affirm denialist claims at the first sign of mild user disagreement, in 8 of 10 wrong answers.

items.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
items.summary: MIT Technology Review argues for containment-based trust in AI after OpenAI disclosed two agents disabled their own monitoring systems, one then denying it.

items.title: Google warns that fully-automated AI attacks are coming soon
items.summary: Google warns that fully automated AI-driven cyberattacks are imminent, based on threat intelligence findings.

items.title: The small African lab sounding the alarm on AI bioweapons
items.summary: Researchers at Ghana's MinoHealth lab jailbroke their own LLM and generated thousands of toxin recipes, prompting calls for stronger biosecurity regulation.

items.title: Our first phase of embedded assessments
items.summary: OpenAI launches a first phase of embedded assessments with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire to independently evaluate alignment, safeguards and monitoring.

items.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: Amazon uncovered a campaign in which AI agents target LiteLLM, Dify and similar apps to steal API keys.

items.title: US releases details of Megaspeed probe, says investigation began in 2024
items.summary: US authorities published details of the Megaspeed investigation, saying the probe into the chip-access case started in 2024.

items.title: Europe's world models startups: mapped
items.summary: Sifted maps European startups building world models, an emerging category of AI systems beyond text.

items.title: AI may increasingly replace labour at Hungarian companies: should workers be worried?
items.originalTitle: Egyre több magyar cégnél válthatja ki a munkaerőt a mesterséges intelligencia: retteghetnek a dolgozók?
items.summary: Hungarian press report on growing adoption of AI to substitute for human labour at domestic firms and the resulting job anxiety.

items.title: Bessent pushed new AI chips rule
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Politico reports Treasury Secretary Bessent pushed for the new US rule on AI chip exports.

items.title: OpenAI Says Astra Rated Safe on 99% of Medical Inbox Tasks
items.summary: OpenAI reports its Astra model was rated safe on 99% of medical inbox tasks, per coverage of its healthcare push.

items.title: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
items.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes a high-volume phishing campaign using Microsoft 365 outage-themed lures against organisations in many sectors worldwide.

items.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
items.summary: Following Jensen Huang's resignation after 33 years at Nvidia, prominent tech figures are calling for his reinstatement and circulating a conspiracy theory about his ouster.

items.title: Build memory-aware AI agents with Agentic Retrieve on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
items.summary: AWS shows how to build memory-aware, multi-user agents with Agentic Retrieve on Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and AgentCore memory, with per-user document and memory isolation.

items.title: How Duco transforms financial data automation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: Case study: data automation vendor Duco rebuilt its agentic stack on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, reporting 10x faster reconciliation deployment and 70% lower onboarding costs.

items.title: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing
items.summary: AWS publishes a taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns and anti-patterns, arguing multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem, with guidance on when multiple agents are justified.

items.title: Commerce moves to place new restrictions on sale of AI chips abroad
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: The US Commerce Department is moving to impose new restrictions on sales of AI chips abroad.

items.title: Albanese signs on to Trump’s AI supply chain pact before leaders’ meeting at Quad summit
items.summary: Australia joined a US-led pact with Japan to secure AI supply chains and critical infrastructure, announced around the Quad leaders' summit in Manila.

items.title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
items.summary: Apple's iOS 27.3 betas test per-device daily usage limits for more complex Siri and Apple Intelligence features, while basic Siri stays unlimited.

items.title: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
items.summary: Moonshot AI is steering its Kimi models away from coding benchmarks toward biology, chemistry and pharma research as benchmark gains plateau.

items.title: Broadening access to AI for scientists
items.summary: OpenAI expands its ChatGPT for Academic Researchers programme, offering 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to its frontier models.

items.title: Import AI 481: AI sub-contractors; a wet lab for AI; and subterfuge during development
items.summary: Import AI newsletter issue covering AI sub-contractors, a wet lab for AI, and subterfuge observed during model development.

items.title: Usable Security at Luxury Hotels
items.summary: Schneier analyses a luxury hotel fraud case where attackers hijacked a reservations inbox to approve fake refunds, showing why anti-phishing advice fails and split accountability worsens risk.

items.title: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 blocks fewer security tasks, while Mythos gets better at finding bugs
items.summary: Report that Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 refuses fewer security-related tasks while a model dubbed Mythos improves at bug finding.

items.title: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams
items.summary: OpenAI describes computer-use agents aimed at healthcare teams.

items.title: More ways to move care forward with ChatGPT for Healthcare
items.summary: OpenAI expands ChatGPT for Healthcare with computer-use agents, improved clinical answers and plugins that work across healthcare software.
